definition_one_sentence: A customer account with at least one non-cancelled order in the last 12 months.
formula_or_rule: count distinct customer_id where status <> 'cancelled' and order_date >= reporting_date - 12 months (rolling)
example: Reporting date 2026-11-25: an account whose last non-cancelled order was on 2026-01-15 is active; one whose only order since 2025-11-25 was cancelled is not.
notes_conflicts: Sales used 6 months and counted cancelled orders; Finance used 12 months, non-cancelled. Decision: 12 months, non-cancelled (comparable year on year for the board). Sales keeps its 6-month view as a separate, named metric 'recently active customer (6 months)' using the same rules, only the window changes; it must never be labelled 'active customer'. Warning: dim_customers.last_order_date currently includes cancelled orders.

definition_one_sentence: What the customer paid for an order after refunds, excluding VAT, shipping fees included.
example: Order of 120.00 EUR incl. VAT and shipping, 24.00 EUR refunded: (120 - 24) / 1.20 = 80.00 EUR net revenue.
notes_conflicts: Sales wanted VAT included (sales team is paid on amounts incl. VAT); Finance requires VAT excluded (VAT is not company money). Decision: net revenue excludes VAT. Sales commissions use 'gross revenue minus refunds' (VAT included), which must be shown under that name, not as net revenue.

definition_one_sentence: A customer account that has ordered before but has no non-cancelled order in the last 12 months.
formula_or_rule: has at least one non-cancelled order ever and no non-cancelled order with order_date >= reporting_date - 12 months
example: Reporting date 2026-11-25: an account whose last non-cancelled order was on 2025-09-01 is churned.
notes_conflicts: Defined as the opposite of active customer so the two always add up. Accounts that never placed a non-cancelled order are neither active nor churned. Used by the churn-prediction ML model (Data Science team).

definition_one_sentence: A customer account registered on ShopFast, identified by customer_id.
formula_or_rule: one row per customer_id in stg_customers / dim_customers
example: Customer 1042 signed up on 2025-03-10; they are a customer even before their first order.
notes_conflicts: A customer is an account, not a person: one person may have several accounts (duplicate emails), so counts of customers may be higher than counts of people.

definition_one_sentence: A purchase placed by a customer, identified by order_id, whatever its status.
formula_or_rule: one row per order_id in fct_orders; status in (pending, shipped, delivered, cancelled, returned)
example: Order 5001 placed on 2026-11-02 by customer 1042, status delivered, 120.00 EUR gross.
notes_conflicts: Cancelled orders are still orders, but they never count towards active customer or churned customer.
